newsitem.title: UK: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - SWISS RE, ART.
newsitem.headline: THE PROTEUS COLUMN - SWISS RE, ART.

text.p: THE PROTEUS COLUMN

Proteus has more than once pointed out the danger of ignoring trends in the alternative risk transfer market. As if to drive the point home, Swiss Re is to issue a statement next week on the likely future of its Alternative Risk Transfer (ART) unit.
Speculation in the Swiss press is that the unit will be spun off and that Credit Suisse will eventually take a share in the new company.

It would be the logical extension of existing arrangements. To strengthen its position in the alternative risk transfer sector, on December 15, 1994, Swiss Re announced a co-operation arrangement with Credit Suisse under which it took a 20% participation in CS Financial Products, a company active in derivatives business. Since then two joint ventures have been started.
And of course former Swiss Re ceo Lukas Muhlemann went on to become group chief of Credit Suisse, allowing head of global alternative risk transfer boss Walter Kielholz to take his place.
These two are certain to be the main drivers of this new development. Kielholz set up the ART division, and had it generating Sfr2 billion by the end of the first year.

And when Muhlemann laid out Swiss Re's global strategy in a presentation to the board in Zurich on October 23, it included forging Swiss Re into a leading provider of alternative risk-transfer covers, with special emphasis on marketing them to captives.

The move is another indication that the ART market is in fact becoming more mainstream. So-called "traditional" companies-such as Liberty Mutual Insurance Cos., American International Group Inc. and United States Fidelity and Guaranty-as well as Swiss Re - expand their capabilities in this area.

And such is the interest that U.S. ratings agency A.M. Best decided recently to expand its rating coverage to alternative risk transfer entities such as risk-retention groups, captives, pools, and self-insurance groups. Coverage of this is available via Reuters Insurance Briefing.
The ART sector is still not about to replace the traditional markets, but those companies which have done nothing to access this lucrative sector may want to take note of the reason ART is growing.

The market began because it could be competitive on price, but increasingly the reasons clients are using them are becoming more strategic. Better claims handling, more effective risk management, greater control over loss prevention and direct access to worldwide reinsurance markets are all cited as advantages of using ART.
If traditional companies cannot compete on these aspects, they may have something to worry about.
